note: The weekly loop's first challengers, from the research (19 Nov 2026): what the research was unsure of, ranked, alternating first-second and look tests.

candidates.test: the bed ~36 dB under the voice against the champion's ~32 dB
candidates.why: the references span 22 dB (KFC) to 36.5 dB (Labubu, Company Man ~36); 32 is a midpoint, not a measurement of what holds viewers

the scan's on-niche Shorts under 35 s have a 54,049 median (81) vs 23,214 at 35-70 s, but the Shorts that broke out (Rise Fall Repeat) run 106-147 s; the build spec asks to test longer; research 2026-11-20 on the same scan: of 151 on-niche English Shorts from the last 60 days, the 19 that beat their channel 3x+ were 1 under 35 s, 5 at 35-60 s, 4 at 60-100 s and 9 at 100-180 s, while the 100-180 s median is only 2,964 views (35-60 s: 15,920): length raises the ceiling, not the median; research 2026-11-22, same scan, correction: Rise Fall Repeat's own split (31 Shorts under 35 s, median 1,406; 80 at 100+ s, median 20,985) is a time effect, not length: its Shorts 120-200 days old got about 1,100-1,300 views at any length (35 under 60 s: 1,323; 10 at 60+ s: 1,048), and only its last 90 days (all 60+ s) grew. Ravate (19.3K subs, English Shorts) in the same age windows: 60-100 s beat under 60 s in 2 of 3 (0-20 days 42,636 vs 28,475; 20-40 days 17,816 vs 9,642; 40-60 days 24,299 vs 28,046). Weak support for longer, not 3x

candidates.test: long videos with no chapter cards (continuous narration with date slams) against 4-5 s chapter cards with a music drop
candidates.why: KFC uses 5 cards and Labubu 9; Modern MBA none; a silent 4-5 s card is also where long-video viewers may leave

candidates.test: a Short whose title and first line ask the question ('Why did everyone stop buying Crocs?') against the champion's paradox claim
candidates.why: the build spec says a claim, never a question, from 4 Rise Fall Repeat Shorts; style.json shows 1 of 4 Shorts opening on a question; thin evidence either way; research 2026-11-23, same scan, each channel's question titles against its own claim titles (English Shorts under 90 days, 5+ of each, 19 channels): the closest business-Shorts channels do worse with questions (Rise Fall Repeat 0.71x, Ravate 0.73x, Signal 404 0.77x, Unravelled by Shankar 0.92x of their claim-title medians), tiny documentary channels better (The Ledger Files 1.38x, Tech & Titans 1.66x, Ascendants 1.63x); median across all 19 is 1.09x and the share of 3x+ breakouts is the same (23% questions, 22% claims, last 30 days). Leans to the champion's claim; our own question title (Tamagotchi, 764 views) is one Short

candidates.test: Shorts with every figure only in the captions (no gold poster card) against the poster card for the one big result
candidates.why: the poster card comes from one channel's Shorts (Rise Fall Repeat); the other references show figures in captions only

candidates.test: long titles of the form 'What Happened to X?' / 'WTF Happened to X?' against a claim title ('Beanie Babies Were Supposed to Pay for College')
candidates.why: the biggest small-channel breakout was 'WTF Happened to Labubu?' (2.28M on 6.5K subs) and 'what happened to brand' is one of the niche's searches; our first titles are mostly claims

candidates.test: stock footage 55-60% with graphics 10-15% (KFC's mix) against the champion's 35-45% footage and 20-25% graphics
candidates.why: KFC ran ~60% stock and ~6% graphics; Fortune & Fall ~40% and ~25%; the champion bets on graphics as our edge, unproven on our own videos

history.test: frame 1 is the document with the figure already highlighted, against the champion's object-first frame (the toy, the cup)
history.why: KFC (591K, the owner's favourite) opens on a report table with a cell highlighted; Labubu (2.28M) and Stanley open on the object. 2 of 3 breakout openings are object-first, so the object is champion; research 2026-11-23, our first Shorts (no stayed-to-watch data yet, views only): the two that opened on a thing the viewer held, stated as a paradox (Stanley's cup 1,139 in 3 days; Tamagotchi 764 within hours), got 17-95x the three that opened on a deal or a payment (the $35 Swoosh 12, Nokia and Microsoft 46, Dollar Shave Club's $4,500 video 38; Toyota vs Mercedes was only hours old). Supports the object-first champion; views only, so not a verdict
